newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - FX volatilities succumb to time decay.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - FX volatilities succumb to time decay.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar-pair options softened under the weight of the weekend time-decay pressure as spot rates drifted toward the middle of their recent ranges, dealers said.
The much awaited February U.S. employment report sparked a brief rally in spot, but the greenback soon lost steam and was unable to sustain bids in volatilities.

"The general feeling is that the market was a little long volatility," said a U.S. bank trader in California. "So, after the employment numbers...also with the Friday effect, volatilities tended to trade off some."
One-month dollar/mark implied volatility dipped below 10 percent to 9.80/9.95 in afternoon U.S. trading from 10.1/10.4 prior to the jobs data.
The dollar/mark volatility curve flattened after being slightly inverted for most of the week.

Traders said shorter-dated options, which have higher rates of time decay, took the blunt of the selling pressure as they had become plump after spot hit 34-month highs above 1.72 marks earlier in the week.
Six-month and one-year volatilities were both little changed at about 9.8/10.0 percent.
Traders said there had been some $1.5 billion worth of very low-delta seven-month mark call selling in the past few days, collecting miniscule premiums.

"This is notable," the California trader said. "Either somebody was long a lot of these stuff and decided to dump it off for whatever they could get, or they're feeling the (spot) market is just not going to go there."

An interbank broker in New York noted, however, that that sale met fairly good buying interest, even though demand for puts and calls in general, as expressed in risk reversals, remained well skewed toward mark puts.
One-month 25-delta dollar/mark risk reversal stood at 0.3/0.6 percent in favor of mark puts.
Dollar/yen volatilities were also pressured at the front end as spot drifted around 122.00 yen, right at the middle of a perceived 120-125 medium-term range, for most of the day.
One-month dollar/yen was a touch below late Thursday levels at 10.5/10.7 percent.

Still, the interbank broker said the back end saw some good bidding, noting that some $200-300 million worth of nine-month 35-delta yen puts and a lot of six-month 20-delta yen calls were sought early on.
"As a result of that, the back end is fairly well bid," he said. The dollar/yen curve was positively sloped, with one-year at 11.0/11.2 percent.
Front-end mark/yen volatilities, which had been well bid all week as spot tested fresh lows, pulled back and flattened the inverted volatility curve as spot rebounded above 71 yen.
One-month mark/yen was assessed at 9.8/10.0 percent, off nearly half a point.
Despite today's rebound, traders said the mark was likely to plumb further lows next week and added that longer-dated low-delta mark puts continued to attract interest.
